Check That No Superassignment Is Used

Source: R/super_assign_check.R
super_assign_check.Rd

Checks that the superassignment operators <<- and ->> are not used in a function. Returns an error with a table of the lines to rewrite if any, since these operators are not allowed in safer-r functions.

Usage

super_assign_check(x, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")

Arguments

x

Function to check, written without quotes and brackets (e.g., fun1 or pkg::fun1).

safer_check

Single logical value. If TRUE (default), checks before running that the required packages and functions are installed and that the classical R operators (like <-) are not masked by another package or by a user-defined object of the global environment. These checks take time at each call: set FALSE in loops and inside other safer-r functions, to avoid repeating them.

lib_path

Vector of character strings: paths of existing extra library folders containing the required packages (e.g., packages installed without admin rights). They are searched after the current .libPaths() during the call (the current libraries keep priority), and .libPaths() is restored on exit. If NULL (default), only the current .libPaths() are used.

error_text

Single character string added to the error messages (e.g., " INSIDE pkg1::fun1()") to name the calling functions. NULL is converted into "".

Value

If no superassignment operator is detected: a message saying that everything seems clean, and NULL, invisibly.

Otherwise: an error, with a table-like message made of one row per reported operator (column 1: line number; column 2: symbol; column 3: code of the line).

Details

Why an error: <<- and ->> assign into the first enclosing environment of the function where the name exists, or into the global environment. What they modify thus depends on where the function is defined, not on its code, and cannot be corrected automatically: rewrite the code, for instance by returning the value, or by using base::assign() with an explicit envir argument.

Reported: every <<- and ->> operator written in the submitted function, also when called as a function (e.g., `<<-`(y, 1) or base::`<<-`(y, 1)), including inside the functions defined in the submitted function (e.g., a FUN argument of base::lapply() or the handlers of base::tryCatch()).

Not reported: the <-, -> and = assignment operators, and the <<- or ->> writings inside strings, comments or backquoted names (e.g., c("<<-") or `a<<-b`), apart from the calls above.

Source references: line 1 is the line of the function keyword. Functions created with options(keep.source = FALSE) (default of Rscript) and functions of installed packages (e.g., saferDev::colons_check) have no source references (attribute srcref): their deparsed code is analyzed, without comments, with line numbers that differ from the source file, and with ->> reported as <<-.

See also

The code checkers of saferDev, in the recommended order of use: super_assign_check, lambda_check, colons_check, all_args_here, curly_bracket_check, true_false_check, for_loop_nb_check (see vignette("saferDev")).

Author

Gael Millot

Examples

# Without source references ("Run examples" link, Rscript), line numbers and comments differ.
# See also https://safer-r.github.io/saferDev/articles/super_assign_check.html
fun1 <- function(x){ y <- x ; base::return(y) }
saferDev::super_assign_check(x = fun1, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL,
    error_text = "") # no superassignment: NULL returned, invisibly
#> 
#> 
#> AFTER RUNNING saferDev::super_assign_check().
#> INSIDE fun1(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN.
#> 
fun2 <- function(x){ y <<- x ; base::return(y) }
base::try(expr = saferDev::super_assign_check(x = fun2, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL,
    error_text = ""), silent = FALSE,
    outFile = base::getOption(x = "try.outFile", default = base::stderr())) # error: <<- reported
#> Error : 
#> 
#> ================
#> 
#> ERROR IN saferDev::super_assign_check().
#> 
#> INSIDE fun2(), THE SUPERASSIGNMENT OPERATORS <<- AND ->> ARE NOT ALLOWED IN SAFER-R FUNCTIONS:
#> PLEASE, REWRITE THE CODE ACCORDINGLY.
#> 
#> LINE	SYMBOL		CODE
#> 3	<<-		y <<- x
#> 
#> ================
#> 
#> 
# A <<- written in a string or in a comment is not an operator: not reported.
fun3 <- function(x){
    y <- "the <<- writing is just a string" # a <<- in a comment
    x
}
saferDev::super_assign_check(x = fun3, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL,
    error_text = "") # no superassignment: NULL returned, invisibly
#> 
#> 
#> AFTER RUNNING saferDev::super_assign_check().
#> INSIDE fun3(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN.
#>
